DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum (likely associated with underlying inflammatory bowel disease and/or neuropathy).

The history of Crohn's disease, the normal infectious workup, and the description of a painful, ulcerative lesion without signs of acute bacterial infection strongly point towards an inflammatory etiology like Pyoderma Gangrenosum rather than an infection or trauma. Can you confirm if the ulcer has a "punched-out" appearance with undermined, violaceous borders, and do you have any history of similar lesions appearing after minor trauma or surgery?
